profile.beat: Long-horizon growth and macro commentary centred on Elliott Wave / 200-week-moving-average setups across US tech, China (BABA), crypto (ETH, BTC, HYPE, BMNR) and silver, plus promotion of a paid Patreon group.
profile.style: Loud, absolute conviction language ('There is only one direction left', 'It is a BUY NOW') built on Elliott Wave counts, Fibonacci targets and buying below the 200 WMA, with occasional fundamental bullets (ETH supply, BABA revenue, insider buys). Heavy victory-lap posting that re-quotes old calls and entry levels. Frames the market as smart money versus retail.
profile.cadence: Very high volume: dozens of one-liners and short multi-line posts a day, many quote-tweets of his own earlier calls, chart teasers with 'IYKYK', motivational aphorisms, and YouTube/Patreon links.
profile.caveats: Selective self-promotion: past calls are re-quoted mainly when they worked, and the account openly says free content exists to hook paid subscribers (2101679531580866806). Many targets are Elliott Wave extrapolations with no stated invalidation, and the author claims to be fully allocated while simultaneously preaching safe havens and warning of a market reset.

narrative: The window opens with the author leaning hard into ETH as it breaks toward his round-number magnet, framing it as a safe haven and a generational hold, with BMNR, COIN and BTC as satellite crypto longs. Through 21-23 September he runs a victory lap on AMD, DELL, ASML, PLTR and HYPE, while flipping to caution on the Wave 5 leaders: NVDA shows a bearish rising wedge, AMD and DELL are called parabolic tops where retail becomes exit liquidity. In their place he pushes hated or pulled-back names — BABA (insider buying, revenue compounding, Wave 2), ASTS (Wave 2 confirmed, connectivity moat), SE and HIMS. From 23-24 September the tone turns macro-defensive: the rising US 10-year, possible Fed hikes and the Iran war lead him to call for rotation into safe havens, with silver repeatedly named as the answer to rising yields and a 'freebie' add for portfolio protection. He describes 'two markets' — one already corrected and offering value, and a narrow tech leadership group yet to correct — and sets explicit lower buy levels for NVDA and NVO rather than chasing.

picks.risk_reward: The author frames buying under the 200 WMA as the risk control and calls it better risk management than leverage; no downside scenario or invalidation level is given.
picks.thesis: Institutional ETF and treasury accumulation, tightening supply from staking and burns, its role as the settlement layer for stablecoins and tokenisation, staking yield, and a completed Wave 2 below the 200 WMA inside a six-year ascending triangle.
